items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ... Rick Rita. I don't think she plays any jazz at all. ... [INTERVIEWEE] I was, uh, uh, I lived on, uh, Benville Street...

ctx.x: Philip. All I knew, the only one I knew who played guitar was, uh, Philip and Sammy.

Well, I think I met that sister. I think her sister is a classical piano player. Rick Rita. I don't think she plays any jazz at all. So, the same one is to teach her? Yeah, I think that's the same one. One is to teach piano? Yeah, yeah, in Washington or something. She's one of the founders of the B-Sharp Music Club. Uh, did, uh, could you tell me where you were when the, uh, Robert Charles riot took place? Do you remember when they killed Robert Charles? Yeah. And he killed all those policemen?

I was, uh, uh, I lived on, uh, Benville Street and I believe I was, uh, that's about thirty, over thirty-five years now. Uh-huh. Yeah, I was living on Benville Street. My first wife would die just then. Uh-huh. Were you playing music then? Yeah, I was playing. Yeah. I was playing with Reddy then. Oh yeah? Yeah, with Robert Charles Wright, you know what? Sure. The mob came up for us, Claiborne and, uh, let's see, it was, uh, Claiborne and Borgias. Uh-huh. And we called, we had the, uh, the battlefield, was called…
